text: Test coil arrangements in eddy current testing. Absolute, differential, and hybrid.

cap: Every probe does two jobs: induce and sense
text: Every eddy current probe does two jobs. It induces eddy currents in the test object, and it senses how the test object reacts to them.

cap: Three families: absolute, differential, hybrid
text: How the coils are arranged to do those two jobs decides what the probe can see, and what it ignores. There are three families of arrangement.

cap: A single coil
text: Start with the absolute arrangement. Zoom in on the probe tip, and you find a single coil.

cap: The same coil induces and senses
text: The same coil is used to induce eddy currents in the test object, and to sense the test object's reaction to those eddy currents.

cap: Tests only the area under the coil, with no comparison
text: It tests only the area under the coil, and it does not compare itself to a reference standard, or to any other part of the test object. Because it tests without a comparison, it is called absolute.

cap: It responds to everything under the coil
text: That means an absolute coil responds to everything under it. Conductivity, permeability, thickness, lift-off, temperature, and discontinuities all move the signal.

cap: Gradual change: slow drift.  Crack: sharp spike.
text: Watch the signal as the coil scans along the part. A gradual change in thickness shows up as a slow drift. A crack shows up as a sharp spike on top of it.

cap: Two coils, connected so their outputs cancel
text: Now the differential arrangement. Two coils are wound and electrically connected, so that the output of one coil cancels the output of the other.

cap: Same properties under both coils: zero output
text: When the test object's properties are the same under both coils, the two outputs cancel, and the instrument reads zero.

cap: The self-comparison technique
text: The test object is being compared with itself, one section against the next. So this is known as the self comparison technique.

cap: Gradual changes reach both coils together and cancel
text: Variables that change gradually affect both coils at the same time, so they cancel. Gradually changing wall thickness, diameter, temperature, and conductivity are not detected.

cap: A short flaw unbalances one coil, then the other
text: But a short discontinuity, like a crack, reaches one coil before the other. First one coil is unbalanced, then the other, and the signal swings one way, and then the opposite way.

cap: Long, uniform flaw: only its two ends give a signal
text: There is a catch. A long flaw of uniform depth can sit under both coils at once. Then only its two ends give a signal.

cap: External comparison: same wiring, two different objects
text: The external comparison technique is wired exactly the same way, except that it is set up on two different objects.

cap: One coil on a reference standard, one on the test object
text: One coil holds an external reference standard. The test object passes through the other coil, and a comparison is made with the standard.

cap: Test object matches the standard: no indication
text: As long as the test object matches the standard, no indication is observed.

cap: A discontinuity unbalances the coils
text: But if a discontinuity appears in the test object, the outputs of the coils become unbalanced, and an indication is obtained.

cap: Gradual changes are no longer hidden
text: The same is true for a change in thickness, permeability, or conductivity, even a gradual one. Nothing is hidden, because the reference never changes.

cap: Mostly used to compare conductivity, permeability and dimension
text: That is why external comparison is mostly used to compare measurements of conductivity, permeability, and dimension.

cap: Hybrid: one coil drives, a separate coil picks up
text: The third family is the hybrid arrangement. Here, one coil drives the eddy currents, and a separate coil picks up the response.

cap: Coils may differ in size and need not be adjacent
text: Hybrid coils may or may not be the same size, and they are not necessarily next to each other. Common types are driver pickup, through transmission, and primary secondary coil assemblies.

cap: Through-transmission: driver on one side, receiver on the other
text: In through transmission, a transmitting, or driver coil, is placed on one side of the material, and induces eddy currents in it. A receiving coil sits on the other side, connected to the indicating instrument.

cap: Coils exactly opposite each other.  Thin materials only.
text: The two coils must be placed exactly opposite each other. And only thin materials may be tested, because the field has to make it through the full thickness.

cap: What sets the voltage in the sensing coil
text: The voltage in the sensing coil depends on the magnitude and frequency of the current applied to the excitation coil, on the parameters of the exciting and sensing coils, and on the characteristics of the test object.

cap: Driver and pickup in the same housing
text: Many other hybrid probes put the driver coil, and the pickup coil or coils, in the same housing. They cannot be called through transmission, but they operate the same way.

cap: Built for specific test geometries
text: They are typically designed and built for very specific test geometries, in an attempt to overcome some of the natural limitations of surface probes.

cap: Aerospace: subsurface cracks and corrosion
text: In the aerospace industry, these probes are common for the detection of subsurface cracks and corrosion.

cap: Which arrangement suits which job?
text: So, which arrangement suits which job?

cap: Absolute: when you want to measure
text: Absolute coils are the choice when you want to measure something. Conductivity measurement and alloy sorting. The thickness of nonconductive coatings. And gradual wall loss from corrosion, which a differential coil would cancel out.

cap: Differential, self-comparison: short, sharp flaws
text: Self comparison differential coils are the choice for finding short, sharp flaws. High speed testing of tube, bar, and wire. Pits and cracks in heat exchanger tubing. And small surface cracks, with far less noise from lift-off and temperature drift.

cap: Differential, external comparison: sorting against a standard
text: External comparison is the choice for sorting. Parts are checked against a known good standard, for alloy, heat treatment, and dimension.

cap: Hybrid: built for the special cases
text: And hybrid coils are built for the special cases. Through transmission for thin sheet and foil. Driver pickup probes for aircraft structure, finding subsurface cracks, and corrosion hidden beneath the surface layer.

cap: Match the arrangement to what you need to find
text: Absolute sees everything under one coil. Differential shows only the difference between two. Hybrid separates driving from sensing. Pick the arrangement that matches what you need to find.
